help.text: 📺 VAR in today's game. In a save that starts in 2026/27, a match can go to a video review from its next kickoff, but only in the competitions we have checked really use VAR this season. Right now that is: Premier League, La Liga, Serie A, Bundesliga, Ligue 1, Eredivisie, Primeira Liga, Scottish Premiership, Süper Lig, Belgian Pro League, Swiss Super League, Austrian Bundesliga, SuperSport HNL, Saudi Pro League, 2. Bundesliga, Champions League. Everything else plays without it until we have checked it too, and the older eras (the 2005, 2010, 2015 and 2020 starts) never get it, even when they run on past 2026. In real football a review can look at goals, penalty calls, red cards (since July 2026 that includes one that came from a clearly wrong second yellow) and a card shown to the wrong player, and the referee's call stands unless it was a clear and obvious error. This game reviews goals and penalties only. In Play Live a goal that gets ruled out goes in first and the check comes after. Then it counts for nothing: no score, no scorer, no shot on the stats. A foul the referee missed can become a penalty, and the kick is a real one that can go in, be saved or miss. You only see a review that changed the call, and it is rare. The numbers come from two published counts of one real season (Serie A 2017/18, its first with VAR), and we took the lower count each time: a goal ruled out about once in 13 matches, a penalty given about once in 11. It works both ways, for you and against you, and it does change results. Example: it is 0-0, a goal is ruled out, then a penalty a review gave is missed. It stays 0-0. Each decision is made once and saved with the match, so the live match and the full time report always agree. Open the match's ? button to read this again.
